summary: Adds encryptQuery / encryptQueryBulk to WasmEncryptionClient in the published @cipherstash/stack/wasm-inline entry (minor changeset). The new methods reuse the native client's resolveIndexType and pre-FFI validators and call two new named imports from @cipherstash/protect-ffi/wasm-inline (pinned 0.29.0, unchanged). The change is additive: existing encrypt/decrypt code paths are untouched, and it does not change storage payloads or SQL. The main release risks are: (1) the new static named imports. If the pinned WASM build did not export them, the whole edge entry would fail to load, including existing encrypt/decrypt. Live Deno e2e tests would catch this, but no CI result was supplied. (2) The declared return type `EncryptedQuery | null` omits the bare string that JSON selector queries return. (3) JSON containment and selector terms are only shape-checked, never row-matched against Postgres. The scalar query types get live row-matching coverage from a new WASM integration suite wired into the Drizzle integration workflow. No test results were seen and none could be run offline (no node_modules, no credentials).

behaviour_changes.description: WasmEncryptionClient gains encryptQuery(plaintext, {table, column, queryType?}) and encryptQueryBulk(terms[]), plus exported types WasmEncryptQueryOptions and WasmQueryTerm. Errors throw rather than returning a Result envelope. null/undefined plaintext returns null without calling ZeroKMS. Bulk is position-stable with null pass-through.

wasm-inline.ts now statically imports encryptQuery and encryptQueryBulk from @cipherstash/protect-ffi/wasm-inline. The protect-ffi version is unchanged (0.29.0) and remains external to dist/wasm-inline.js, so consumers resolve it from npm or an import map. If the export is missing, the import fails when the module links.

Index-type resolution and value validation on the WASM path reuse the native client's resolveIndexType, assertValidNumericValue and assertValueIndexCompatibility. The behaviour includes the ore->ope swap for v3 _ord domains, equality answered via the ordering index, and ste_vec queryOp inferred from the value's shape (a string becomes a selector, anything else a containment term). queryOp is omitted, not set to undefined, because WASM serde rejects undefined fields. The native path passes unverifiedContext audit metadata; the WASM path does not.

CI: integration-drizzle.yml now triggers on packages/stack/src/wasm-inline.ts and adds integration/wasm/** to CS_IT_SUITE, on both the postgres and supabase matrix legs. The integration vitest config re-aliases the wasm-inline FFI and auth specifiers to the real modules in node_modules. The Deno e2e tests now fail instead of skipping when CS_* credentials are missing, and a new query-types Deno test is picked up by `deno task test`.

The shipped JSDoc on encryptQuery says query terms are ciphertext-free and therefore "safe to log-scrub less aggressively than storage payloads". It also documents raw-SQL cast recipes (`$n::jsonb::eql_v3.query_<domain>`).

failure_scenarios.title: Missing WASM export breaks the whole wasm-inline entry, including existing encrypt/decrypt
failure_scenarios.trigger: The resolved @cipherstash/protect-ffi/wasm-inline build does not export encryptQuery or encryptQueryBulk. This could happen with the pinned 0.29.0 build, or with a consumer import map or override that resolves a different version.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: wasm-inline.ts:78-85 statically imports encryptQuery and encryptQueryBulk alongside the existing encrypt/decrypt imports. In ESM, a missing named export is a link-time SyntaxError for the whole module, not a failure only when the new methods are called. protect-ffi is external to the bundle, so the exports come from whatever the consumer resolves. The dependency version did not change in this diff, and the package contents could not be inspected.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Any edge consumer upgrading @cipherstash/stack fails to import @cipherstash/stack/wasm-inline at all, which breaks existing encrypt/decrypt. The failure is loud. The npm release cannot be reversed, so it would need a new release.

failure_scenarios.title: JSON containment/selector terms never row-matched in SQL; a wire mismatch would silently return no rows
failure_scenarios.trigger: An edge consumer uses queryType 'searchableJson' (or inference on a Json column) and binds the term into eql_v3 containment (`@>` with ::eql_v3.query_jsonb) or `->`/`->>` selector SQL
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The WASM integration adapter's SUPPORTED_OPS covers only scalar ops (eq/ne/in/notIn/range/matches/order/null). JSON containment and selector are never executed against Postgres. The Deno query-types test only asserts the shape: `{sv:[...]}` with no `v` or `c` for containment, and a non-empty string for the selector. If the WASM build's ste_vec term did not match what the installed EQL v3 SQL expects (for example, selector hashing that differs from the stored sv entries), the query would succeed and match nothing.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Encrypted JSON searches on the edge silently return empty or incomplete result sets. Callers may treat this as "no match" (for example, authorization lookups or dedup checks). Only adopters of the new API are affected, and stored data is not.

failure_scenarios.title: Declared return type omits the bare-string selector result, so typed consumer code mis-handles it
failure_scenarios.trigger: A consumer calls encryptQuery or encryptQueryBulk with a string value on a Json column (searchableJson selector) and handles the result according to its declared type
failure_scenarios.mechanism: encryptQuery is declared to return Promise<EncryptedQuery | null> (wasm-inline.ts:443), and encryptQueryBulk to return Array<EncryptedQuery | null> (wasm-inline.ts:479). EncryptedQuery is CipherStashEncryptedQuery | CipherStashEncryptedV3Query (types.ts:72-74). However, the head's own JSDoc (wasm-inline.ts:418) and Deno test say the selector path returns a bare string, and the test has to cast `as unknown as string`. The native API's result type includes `| string` (types.ts:333); the WASM one does not. The wasm-inline sources are excluded from the package's typecheck, and the Deno test runs with --no-check, so nothing type-tests the published .d.ts.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Consumer code narrows the result with `'v' in term` or `'k' in term`, as types.ts:59 recommends, and gets a runtime TypeError, because the `in` operator throws on a string primitive. Alternatively, it binds the result as `$n::jsonb::eql_v3.query_jsonb` and gets a Postgres error. The failure is loud and confined to new adopters, but it is a published type contract that has to change later.

failure_scenarios.title: Shipped guidance encourages laxer logging of deterministic query terms
failure_scenarios.trigger: Edge consumers follow the encryptQuery JSDoc and log query terms more freely than storage payloads
failure_scenarios.mechanism: wasm-inline.ts:371-374 says terms are "safe to log-scrub less aggressively than storage payloads". Equality (unique/HMAC) and ORE/OPE terms are derived from the plaintext and, for equality, are deterministic per column. Logged terms can therefore be correlated with stored index terms to link log lines to rows or to infer frequencies.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Encrypted-search metadata leaks into application logs or third-party log sinks, which weakens the encryption guarantees customers rely on. This is not plaintext exposure. The cause is the documentation, not code behaviour.
missing_verification: Security or docs review of the shipped wording
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Reword the JSDoc to say that query terms should be treated as sensitive: they are ciphertext-free but plaintext-derived and linkable.
